title: Color, contrast, and theming
summary: Choose text and background colors that meet contrast needs and use CSS variables.

scenario.briefing: The product card uses light gray text on white, which many users cannot read. Replace it with a high-contrast token and keep the accent for actions only.

hints: Use a dark text color on white, such as #000 or #222.
Define colors as CSS variables in :root.
Reserve the accent color for actions.
Set :root { --text: #000; --paper: #fff; --accent: #B54131; } and .card { color: var(--text); background: var(--paper); }.

misconceptions.description: Using color alone to convey meaning.
misconceptions.testDescription: Body text uses a high-contrast color.
misconceptions.feedback: Color alone is not enough; add text or icons. Also ensure sufficient contrast.

misconceptions.description: Believing contrast is only a visual preference.
misconceptions.feedback: Low contrast excludes users with low vision. Contrast is an accessibility requirement, not decoration.

sections.title: Contrast
sections.body: Text must stand out from its background. Light gray on white is hard to read. Use dark text on light backgrounds and check contrast ratios.

sections.title: Theming with variables
sections.body: CSS custom properties in :root define a palette. Components reference variables instead of hard-coded colors, making themes consistent and changeable.

vocabulary.definition: The luminance difference between text and background.
A custom property that stores a reusable value.
A color used sparingly to highlight actions.
